title: Rental security deposit not returned
scope_note: Covers a tenant trying to recover a security deposit after vacating. Does NOT cover eviction, rent increase disputes, or landlord claims for large damage (those need a lawyer).

field_labels.vacated_date: the date you vacated and handed over the keys
field_labels.what_happened: what the landlord said or did about returning it (and any deductions claimed)
field_labels.proof: what proof you have (rent agreement, payment proof, chats, key-handover message)
field_labels.state: which state/city the property is in

limitation.note: Three years is the general period for money claims; the exact start date can depend on the agreement, so a lawyer should confirm.

provisions.title: Deposit cap and refund (only where the state has adopted it)
provisions.plain: The Model Tenancy Act caps a residential security deposit at 2 months' rent (6 months for commercial) and says the deposit is refunded when the landlord takes back vacant possession, after deducting lawful dues. BUT it is a model law: it applies only in a state that has adopted it, so many tenants are governed by their state's own rent law and the rent agreement.
provisions.caveat: Do not tell the user the cap applies without knowing their state has adopted the Act.

provisions.title: Time limit
provisions.plain: Money claims such as recovering a deposit generally have a limitation period of 3 years. The start date can depend on what the agreement says, so confirm with a lawyer if the claim is old.
provisions.caveat: Specific Article numbers are disputed across sources; the assistant must NOT cite an Article number.

provisions.title: Where to go
provisions.plain: In a state that has adopted the Model Tenancy Act, a Rent Authority/Rent Court may hear deposit disputes. Elsewhere, the usual route is a civil suit for recovery of money (often in the civil or small-causes court). A consumer commission is usually not the right forum against a private landlord. Interest: there is generally no fixed statutory rate for private deposits; you can ask for reasonable interest in the notice and suit.
provisions.caveat: Single secondary source; keep wording hedged.

procedure.title: Typical path
steps: Gather proof: rent agreement, proof of paying the deposit, chats about vacating, photos of the flat at handover.
Ask the landlord in writing (WhatsApp/email) for the refund with a date.
Send a legal notice (draft provided) by registered post/speed post and email, giving about 15 days.
If still unpaid: Rent Authority (if your state adopted the Model Tenancy Act) or a civil suit for recovery. Legal aid (NALSA 15100) can help if cost is a problem.
Keep all proof of posting and delivery.
